title: Louis XIII to Brulart de Leon, ambassador in Venice, 15 Sep 1615 and 25 Jul 1617, BnF fr. 18043 f. 83-84 and fr. 18044 f. 109-110 (DECODE R2785, R2786)

steps.what: Fetched the DECODE record views for R2785 and R2786, one image of each and the key file with the shared cookie.

Checked Tomokiyo's louisxiii.htm (DECODE's pointer): the Brulart de Leon cipher of 1615-18 reconstructed by him, both letters read with it (DECODE 'Partially decrypted', 2021); the residue probably nulls or cancelled signs. Entry closed without applying the key.

Split from the former combined target louis1615 (catalogue 191) under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R2785/R2786 (the Brulart de Leon cipher, Tomokiyo's key) and R2748 (the 1631 Sabran cipher, Lasry's solution) are different ciphers. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps kept as recorded.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Tomokiyo's readings linked by URL (DECODE R2785, R2786; cryptiana louisxiii.htm); no transcription or local decryption exists in the repository (project work).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): no text of R2785 or R2786 is in the repository, and cryptiana louisxiii.htm gives the key and remarks on undeciphered symbols, not the letters. Both relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read; method read from existing decipherment -> not solved.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b17): every file on DECODE R2785 and R2786 fetched with the shared cookie into the session scratchpad (b17_fetch.py): 4 page images each and Tomokiyo's key png; no transcription or plaintext attached. Both letters carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment over most cipher runs.

Clear text and interlinear decipherments of R2785 (ff. 83r-84r) and R2786 (ff. 109r-110r) transcribed from native-resolution strips (b17_crop.py); each cipher run aligned with its decipherment and checked against Tomokiyo's key (texts/R2785_align.tsv, R2786_align.tsv): the numbers (20 de, 5 pre, 7 que, 8 qui, 18 con, 30 tion, 35 en, 97 pour ...) and letter signs carry the glosses throughout. R2785 is dated 16 Sept 1615.

θ (not in Tomokiyo's table) is a null: R2786 'ff ʃʃ θ' = 'et', and it falls between words wherever it occurs; R2786 f. 109v row 8 the figures give 'inconvenients' where the decipherer wrote 'incommoditez'; row 11 (no gloss) decodes 'en mesme temps'.

Unglossed spaced-sign lines (R2785 f. 83v rows 17-18, f. 84r row 2; R2786 f. 109v rows 9-11 in part) decoded with the key, with and without θ and φ as nulls: no French; consistent with Tomokiyo's note that they may be nulls.
Readings and translations written (texts/R2785_reading.md, R2786_reading.md, _en.md); clean-sentence share on the bodies 0.854 and 0.863. Both set read (grade B).

Consistency pass (cl): class read failed the read bar (documents R2785 and R2786 read in part: R2785's ~60 spaced signs and R2786 f. 109v rows 9-11 unread, three glosses illegible) -> class read in part. The siblings escalation step (other Brûlart letters in fr. 18043/18044) was identified but not opened: unticked, target stays in progress.

Siblings escalation step. DECODE neighbours R2782-R2789 opened with the project cookie: R2782/R2783 Mazarin to Le Tellier 1652 (Le Tellier-Colbert cipher 2), R2784 no record, R2787 Villeroi to Henri III 1577, R2788/R2789 Catherine de Medicis and Charles IX to du Croc 1567: none related. Gallica (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF; view = folio + 1 in fr. 18043, + 5 in fr. 18044) leaves next to the two letters: fr. 18043 f. 80v (end of a clear French report, 8 Oct 1615), ff. 81r-82r (clear Spanish copies of the Marques de la Hinojosa's letters from Milan to Claudio Marini, Sept-Oct 1615), ff. 85r-86r (Puysieux's autograph clear letter to Leon, Poitiers 'x6' Sept 1615: Mantua's harshness to his rebels, Marini to retire to Genoa, 'M. Mansau qui est a Rome' to go to Savoy, the princess's illness), ff. 87r-v (a further Louis XIII letter to Leon, Poitiers late Sept 1615, in the same cipher with a full interlinear decipherment; not on DECODE); fr. 18044 ff. 107r-108r (Puysieux's clear letter, Paris 26 July 1617: Venice, the Savoy accord, Lesdiguieres, Don Pedro), ff. 111r-v (Puysieux's autograph clear letter, Paris 25 July 1617: Gueffier's arrival, the Grisons, 'la retraitte du Padavin'). No decipherment or key of the residue. Applied: R2785 '[?Manjeaux]' -> Manseau and R2786 '[?Padavin]' -> Padavin (confirmed by the Puysieux letters); R2785's spaced-sign lines judged nulls (no gloss, no French under the key, doubled signs, the clear sentence closes over them, f. 87 has none) and left out of the reading. read_share 0.962 -> 0.971 (R2785), 0.959 -> 0.961 (R2786); v2_score explicit holes 0.902 -> 0.927 and 0.902. R2786 rows 9-11 and the three R2785 glosses stay open.

outcome.method_basis: Both letters read on 22 Oct 2026 from the contemporary interlinear decipherments written over their cipher runs, transcribed from the DECODE images and checked run by run against Satoshi Tomokiyo's reconstructed key (DECODE DOC_2785/2786); one unglossed run (en mesme temps, R2786 f. 109v) decoded with his key.
outcome.notes: Tomokiyo leaves some symbols undeciphered (probably nulls or cancelled signs, per his DECODE notes); not re-checked here. Nothing new about the text. Catalogue entry 191 removed 21 Sept 2026. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no plaintext of either letter exists in the repository or on Tomokiyo's page; both decoded, not read; class already solved -> not read, method -> not solved. 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b17): both letters read from their contemporary interlinear decipherments, checked against Tomokiyo's key (texts/); θ is a null; R2785 is dated 16 Sept 1615.

credits.note: key of the Brulart de Leon cipher (1615-18) reconstructed; R2785 and R2786 read with it, residue probably nulls
interlinear decipherment above most cipher runs of the R2785 text page

texts.label: Poitiers, 16 Sep 1615
texts.summary: Louis XIII, countersigned by Brûlart de Sillery, to Léon Brûlart, his ambassador in Venice: clear French with cipher runs (contemporary decipherments above them mention 'Marini', 'retirer a Gennes', 'domestiques', 'aucun ombrage'); the King is still held in the town by his eldest sister's illness, which fits the court at Poitiers in September 1615. The reading is Satoshi Tomokiyo's, with his key, on DECODE R2785 and cryptiana louisxiii.htm.

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b17): clear text and the contemporary interlinear decipherment transcribed from the DECODE images (ff. 83r-84r), every run checked against Tomokiyo's key (texts/R2785_align.tsv); _check_reading.py on the body 0.854 (35/41). Open: three spaced-sign lines with no decipherment that give no French under the key (probably nulls, as Tomokiyo noted) and three cramped glosses on f. 83v. Dated 16 (not 15) Sept 1615.

texts.label: Paris, 25 Jul 1617
texts.summary: Louis XIII (countersigned Brûlart de Sillery) to Léon Brûlart, ambassador in Venice; read by Satoshi Tomokiyo with his reconstructed Brûlart de Léon key (1615-18). Its contents are not described in the repository; only the address leaf was fetched.

reading_review.note: Read 22 Oct 2026 (b17): clear text and the contemporary interlinear decipherment transcribed from the DECODE images (ff. 109r-110r), checked against Tomokiyo's key; 'incommoditez' corrected to the figures' 'inconvenients', and the unglossed 'en mesme temps' decoded with the key (texts/R2786_align.tsv); _check_reading.py on the body 0.863 (44/51). Open: most of f. 109v rows 9-11 and 110r row 1 (no decipherment, no French under the key) and the figures 16, 21 of row 8.

gaps.item: R2786 f. 109v rows 9-11 / f. 110r row 1 outside the glossed words (R2785's three spaced-sign lines were judged nulls on 23 Oct 2026 and left out of its reading; see NOTES)
gaps.detail: no contemporary decipherment, no French under Tomokiyo's key with or without θ and φ as nulls, and the siblings checked 23 Oct 2026 (Puysieux's clear letters of 25 and 26 July 1617, fr. 18044 ff. 111r-v and 107r-108r) give the sense of the Savoy paragraph but not its words; Tomokiyo's DECODE notes take such passages for nulls or cancelled signs

gaps.item: R2785 f. 83v: three cramped interlinear glosses ('m'est possible', '[?lors] de [?propos]', 'l'Equidray') and the gloss after 'ont este'
gaps.detail: the decipherer's hand is small and blotted at the resolution of the DECODE photographs; the letter signs under them are partly ambiguous in the key (the circled sign is l or y); the Gallica full-resolution images (23 Oct 2026) are no clearer, and no sibling letter repeats these clauses

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, re-read (b17): both documents of outcome.texts read (2 of 2). The unread pieces inside them (R2785's three spaced-sign lines, about 60 signs, probably nulls; parts of R2786 f. 109v rows 9-11) are named in gaps. 23 Oct 2026 (siblings pass): R2785's spaced-sign lines judged nulls and left out of the reading; read_share by v10_relabel.share 0.971 (R2785) and 0.961 (R2786). 23 Oct 2026 (cl): the 1.0 counts documents whose sentences read; it is not a share of signs: both documents stay read in part (documents[].read) because of those passages, so the class is read in part.

prior.where: DECODE R2785/R2786 (Tomokiyo, Aug 2021) and cryptiana louisxiii.htm "Brulart de Leon"
